business_problem: Accenture needed an enterprise-wide digital core that could unify data across major systems, support faster decisions, and make it practical to scale AI and generative AI use cases across a complex global business.
solution_summary: Accenture rebuilt its internal technology landscape around what it calls a digital core: an interconnected cloud, data, and AI foundation that integrates SAP, Workday, and Salesforce into a real-time enterprise data layer. Leaders consume that data through 360 Value Navigator for drill-down performance views and scenario planning, while AI capabilities are layered on top to improve decision support and productivity. The architecture is largely cloud-based and intentionally composable so SaaS tools can be added or replaced without recreating the estate. Accenture also set up an integrated generative AI hub and center-of-excellence model to coordinate use cases, training, and delivery across the business. Copilot for Microsoft 365 and other AI capabilities are already deployed on top of this foundation, and partner technologies such as the Identity Trust Engine and SAP finance analytics extend the model into security and simulation workflows. The result is an operating core that turns shared enterprise data into governed AI-enabled workflows rather than isolated functional systems.

business_outcome: Accenture reduced fragmentation across enterprise systems, gave leaders real-time cross-functional visibility, and created a reusable foundation for AI-driven productivity, scenario planning, and operating-model reinvention.
